analysis.title: Short Squeeze Alert? Hedge Fund Short Leverage Nears 5-Year High As Pros Dump Tech At Record Pace
key_insights: Hedge funds net sold global equities month to date through Oct 19, with short sales outpacing long buys about 5 to 1. Long leverage is in the 73rd percentile over 1 year (94th over 5 years). Short leverage is in the 99th percentile, near 5-year highs.

Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 5.4 points in October to 211.9% (66th percentile 1-year, 89th percentile 3-year). Net leverage fell 3.1 points to 49.4%, the 1st percentile over 1 year and 4th percentile over 3 years. Managers are running as much capital as before with far less directional exposure.

Beta-adjusted Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 8.7 points in the week of Oct 12-16 (-3.8 standard deviations on a 5-year basis) and 10.9 points month over month. Goldman calls it one of the sharpest declines in its data sets. The only comparable four-week drops since 2018 were April 2025 (Liberation Day) and January 2021.
Beta-adjusted net leverage remains higher than the unadjusted measure in both absolute and percentile terms, so hedge funds are less defensive than the raw numbers suggest.

Goldman's Global Fundamental L/S estimate is down 2.5% in October (+10.1% YTD, versus a peak of about 17-18% in late June), after -0.55% in September. Fundamental L/S alpha is down 1.4% MTD (+6.9% YTD), driven by long-side losses. Systematic L/S funds are +0.65% MTD and +20.5% YTD.

By strategy and region, TMT L/S funds are down 7.4% MTD (+10.2% YTD), Asia L/S funds down 6.3% (+17.1% YTD, up about 40% in late June), Health Care L/S down 6.1% (+3.9% YTD), and US funds down 1.6% (+6.8% YTD).

Every major region except Europe (modestly net bought) was net sold in October, led by North America and EM Asia. Asia's overweight versus MSCI ACWI fell from about 20 points over the summer to 11-12 points. North America remains a large underweight.

Within Asia, Taiwan, Japan and Korea were the most net sold markets MTD, while Australia and Hong Kong were the most net bought. Korea's share of global net exposure fell to 3.3% from a peak of about 8% in June, the lowest since early February. Taiwan is near 6.5%.

Global Info Tech saw the largest two-week percentage net selling in Goldman's 10+ year record (Oct 5-16, -3.3 standard deviations), from both long and short sales. Net allocation to Goldman's Global AI basket (GSXGGLAI) fell to the 38th percentile over 1 year, and its long/short ratio fell to the 6th percentile.

Mag 7 net allocation rose to a record, around 22% of total US net exposure, as mega cap net flows stayed resilient. The gap between US Semis & Semi Equipment and Software net exposure narrowed from about 12 points in the spring to about 3 points.

Consumer Discretionary, Materials, Energy and Financials were among the most net sold US sectors MTD. Health Care, Real Estate and Staples were among the most net bought. The long/short ratio on Goldman's US Cyclicals basket (GSXUCYCL) is in the 5th percentile, near 3-year lows, which Goldman reads as more caution on growth.

Within Consumer Discretionary, selling came through short sales, with Hotels/Restaurants/Leisure, Broadline Retail and Household Durables the most net sold subsectors. Staples buying was driven by short covers.

Health Care risk has been unwound for five consecutive weeks, led by Biotech de-grossing since mid-August. Goldman thinks the Biotech de-grossing is in the late innings, as selling shifted from long sales to short covers. The Biotech long/short ratio is about 3.2, down from above 5 in January.

Net exposure to Medium-Term Momentum is on track to fall for a 5th straight month to the lowest since June 2025 (still the 73rd percentile on a 5-year basis, down from about 60% of fund equity at the peak to about 25%). Net exposure to Profitability jumped to 5-year highs as managers favor higher quality names.

Goldman's Dioni Ellinikaki says the data fits the view that hedge funds reduced tilts and directional bias rather than derisking outright, with gross elevated and net much lower. Global AI positioning is down meaningfully, Mag 7 positioning is at an all-time high, and Semis vs Software exposures are narrowing.

The article names two break scenarios. If the tape keeps falling, gross at the 89th percentile leaves a lot of de-grossing ahead. If the tape turns, near-record short books become squeeze fuel. The author's view is that near-term risk skews to the upside.

Market context on Oct 22: the S&P 500 rose 0.58% to 7,757 and the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.1%. The VIX fell to 16.7 and the S&P is about 1.1% below its Oct 6 peak. The 10Y yield is 5.12%. Goldman's desk saw buyers of short-dated upside in size, including $18M premium on SPY Nov 800 and Dec 810 calls, and views right-tail hedges as historically cheap. Meta rose 5% after hours on a Q3 beat.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The hot print and renewed doubts about AI capex payoff triggered the unwind in semis and AI infrastructure that began in Asian memory stocks.
The yield level sits alongside record-low hedge fund net exposure. The author reads it as a sign of how little the pros trust the market apart from the Mag 7.

trade_ideas.description: Buy short-dated upside calls on SPY (Nov 800 and Dec 810 strikes), as observed in Goldman desk flow and not as a Goldman recommendation
trade_ideas.rationale: The desk notes that with positioning increasingly defensive, right-tail hedges are historically cheap.

risk_factors: Gross leverage at the 89th percentile (3-year) leaves a large de-grossing ahead if the tape keeps falling, with longs sold and shorts covered together.
Near-record short books could produce a squeeze if the tape turns, especially as earnings beat and buybacks return.
Mag 7 crowding at a record is a concentration risk, with the AI trade effectively reduced to seven stocks.
Renewed doubts over the payoff from AI capex and a hot CPI print drove the semis unwind.
Cyclicals shorting and the 5th percentile cyclicals long/short ratio point to hedge fund worry over the growth outlook.
A retail handoff into leveraged semis (a record $7B into a 3x semis ETF) adds risk if semis fall further.

tension_points.bull_case: Short leverage is in the 99th percentile and net leverage in the 1st percentile. Buyers of short-dated upside are active, right-tail hedges are cheap, Meta's Q3 beat is a catalyst, and the S&P is only about 1.1% below its Oct 6 peak. Crowded short books could be forced to cover.
tension_points.bear_case: Gross leverage at the 89th percentile (3-year) is a lot of risk to unwind. If the tape keeps falling, de-grossing (selling longs and covering shorts together) still lies ahead.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A continued fall in the tape that triggers de-grossing of the elevated gross book.
